concept.name: Gap down
concept.definition: A gap in which a session's high is lower than the previous session's low, leaving an untraded void above the new session's range. Generally read as a sign of strong selling pressure; its analytical meaning depends on where in the trend or pattern it occurs.
concept.intuition: Supply overwhelmed demand overnight, so the market had to reopen below yesterday's entire trading range.
concept.mechanics: Identified when today's high falls below yesterday's low. Interpretation follows gap typology: common gap inside congestion, breakaway gap on a range breakdown, runaway gap mid-downtrend, or exhaustion gap late in an extended decline.
concept.failure_modes: Gap downs late in a decline can be exhaustion gaps that mark capitulation lows; intraday-only gaps that do not hold into the close carry no structural significance.
concept.misconceptions: That a gap down guarantees further downside; panic gap downs are frequently filled quickly as the selling exhausts itself.
concept.example: A stock in a trading range gaps below range support on heavy volume after a profit warning — a bearish breakaway-style gap down.

citations.source: StockCharts ChartSchool — Gaps and Gap Analysis
